visual_elements.description: 2D multi-class classification plot with x and y axes, arrowheads at the positive ends, and no visible axis labels. Three classes are shown: C1 as green dots clustered in the upper area, C2 as blue dots clustered on the right, and C3 as red dots clustered in the lower-left. Three linear decision boundaries are shown: a red line labeled "d1(x)" running upper-left to lower-right, an unlabeled blue line running lower-left to upper-right, and a green line labeled "d3(x)" running lower-left to upper-right with a shallower slope. Hatched shading separates the background regions. Yellow boxes labeled "C1", "C2", and "C3" sit near their respective clusters. Four orange boxes each contain "?" and are positioned left-middle, center, upper-right, and bottom-center. Three black "+ve" labels appear near the green arrow on the left, the blue arrow at the top-right, and the red arrow at the bottom-right. Leader lines connect the "Undefined" box to plot regions.
Slide number indicator: white circle with purple outline containing black number "8".
Light blue-green rectangular box with dark border containing "Undefined". Thin leader lines extend from the box to regions inside the plot.
Purple rectangular box with dark border containing "New Class".

recreation_brief:
1. Set the full slide background to light gray (#e6e6e6).
2. At the top center, place one bold sans-serif title line: "Multi-Class Classification using " in red (#c0392b), "[ONE VS ALL]" in blue (#21618c), and " Binary Classifiers" in red (#c0392b).
3. At the top-right corner, draw a white circle (#ffffff) with a purple outline (#8e44ad) and center the black text "8" inside it.
4. In the center, draw a white rectangle (#ffffff) with a red border (#c0392b), extending vertically from approximately 20% to 92% of the slide height and spanning most of the slide width.
5. Inside the plot, draw black x and y axes with arrowheads at the positive ends; add no axis text labels.
6. Add three clusters of circular dots: green dots (#2ecc71) for C1 in the upper plot area, blue dots (#2980b9) for C2 in the right plot area, and red dots (#c0392b) for C3 in the lower-left plot area.
7. Draw three straight decision boundaries: a red line (#c0392b) from upper-left to lower-right labeled "d1(x)"; an unlabeled blue line (#2980b9) from lower-left to upper-right; and a green line (#27ae60) from lower-left to upper-right with a shallower slope than the blue line, labeled "d3(x)".
8. Place three yellow rectangles (#f1c40f) with bold black text: "C1" beside the upper green cluster, "C2" beside the right blue cluster, and "C3" beside the lower-left red cluster.
9. Place four orange rectangles (#e67e22), each containing one black "?", at left-middle, center, upper-right, and bottom-center within the plot.
10. Add exactly three black "+ve" text labels: one near the green arrow on the left, one near the blue arrow at the top-right, and one near the red arrow at the bottom-right.
11. Apply hatched shading to the background regions between the three decision boundaries, keeping the dots, lines, and labels visible above the shading.
12. Outside the plot at the top-left, place a light blue-green rectangle (#d5f5e3) with a dark border and the black text "Undefined"; draw thin leader lines from this box into the plot regions.
13. Outside the plot at the middle-right, place a light purple rectangle (#d7bde2) with a dark purple border (#8e44ad) and the black text "New Class".
